html:
The Kayabí, or Kaiabi, are an Indigenous people of northern Mato Grosso in Brazil, speaking a Tupi-Guarani language related to those of the Tupi of the coast. Their old home lay along the Teles Pires and Arinos rivers, where the map places them in 1492.

In the early 1900s rubber tappers of the rubber boom moved onto their land, bringing violence and disease. In the 1950s and 1960s the Villas-Bôas brothers persuaded many Kayabí to move into the new Xingu Indigenous Park, created in 1961, where most of them live today alongside other peoples. Others stayed on a reserve to the west, on the border of Pará. They are known for their fine basketry.
